newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian anti-trust body blasts petrol pump market.
newsitem.headline: Italian anti-trust body blasts petrol pump market.

text.p: Italian service stations are pumping up their petrol prices in an artificial market which is dominated by state-controlled energy giant ENI, the anti-trust watchdog said in a report published on Wednesday.
The Italian anti-trust commission, headed by former prime minister Giuliano Amato, launched its enquiry into petrol price rises in April.
Presenting the findings at a news conference, Amato said that following liberalisation of the market two years ago, prices were now virtually identical between the various distibution outlets.

"This is not because we have a market where there is perfect competition but the exact opposite," Amato said, blaming the strong market position held by ENI's distribution arm, Agip, for much of the price distortion.
"Agip is the only company with a nationwide network and the contracts other companies have to use Agip's depots means that final prices are built around a homogenous base," Amato said.
He urged the government to intervene and create a more competitive environment. The anti-trust commission has no independent powers to enact its own recommendations.

To illustrate the market distortions, Amato said more efficient distribution companies were enjoying a net margin of around 54.4 lire ($0.36) per litre. The less efficient companies had net margins of just 12.6 lire.
A litre of unleaded petrol costs around 1,850 lire at most Italian service stations.
"We already have the margins for a fall in prices and imagine what positive effect that could have on inflation," Amato said.
